title: Autonomous Optimize: idempotent apply adapter & webhook reconciliation
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a resilient API + webhook adapter that lets Optimize automation safely propose and apply batching/caching configuration recommendations. The goal is idempotent apply semantics, bounded retries, and deterministic reconciliation so automation clients (Optimize service + third-party orchestrators) can safely roll forward and roll back without causing cascading conflicts or customer-facing incorrect configs.

Goals:
- Define an HTTP API endpoint for 'propose' and 'apply' that is idempotent by token and operation hash.
- Create a webhook adapter for external systems (Console, Dedicated control plane) to receive apply confirmations and reconcile failures.
- Implement optimistic concurrency with deterministic merge rules and automated rollback on partial failures.
- Provide SDK helper primitives for retries, backoff, and conflict resolution.

Design (high level):
- Propose flow: POST /optimize/v1/recommendations with payload (rec_id, target_route, changes, score, op_hash). Returns 202 and holding resource.
- Apply flow: POST /optimize/v1/apply with idempotency_key and op_hash. Server responds 200 if op already applied, 202 if in progress, 409 on conflict.
- Webhooks: /webhooks/optimize-events sends events: apply.requested, apply.succeeded, apply.failed, apply.rolled_back. Each event includes op_hash, idempotency_key, timestamp, and a compact change-set diff.

Idempotency & Reconciliation rules:
- Apply must be idempotent using idempotency_key (client-supplied UUID v4). Same key + op_hash => operation deduplicated. If same key but different op_hash => reject 400 (client error).
- Server maintains applied_ops table with op_hash, idempotency_key, route, status, result_meta, created_at. TTL of 90 days for auditing.
- Conflicts detected if the target route has a newer config_version > op_base_version. In that case apply enters 'conflict' state and the webhook adapter sends apply.failed (conflict). Client can call apply?force or rebase flow — but force requires explicit human approval via Console.

Retry semantics:
- Clients should retry idempotent applies on 5xx and network errors up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff (initial 500ms).
- On 409, do not retry automatically; surface to operator unless operation includes a rebase_hint.

Edge cases and safety guarantees:
- Partial GPU pool application: when applying to Dedicated pools that roll across N pods, the adapter will orchestrate a stepwise rollout (batch size configurable) and emit per-step events. On >20% step failures we auto-trigger rollback and emit apply.rolled_back.
- Schema validation: strong JSON schema with strict types. Invalid payloads produce 422 with detailed errors.

SDK primitives (v0.6):
- applyRecommendation(rec, idempotencyKey, opts) => returns applyPromise with status stream, retries built-in, and hooks for onConflict, onRollback.
- watchApply(opId, listener) => subscribes to server-sent events for progress.
- reconcileLocalState(route, op_hash) => helper that fetches current config and suggests rebase operations.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Spike completed 2025-02-20 (spike notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/optimize/idempotency-spike).
- Unit + integration tests in optimize-service and controlplane mocks. End-to-end tests using Dedicated staging pool (testbed: dedicated-staging-3).
- Canary rollout: enable API for internal customers, then opt-in early adopters. Feature flag: ff.optimize.idempotent-apply.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- New dashboard: Optimize > Automation > Apply Success Rate (5m, 1h), Conflict Rate, Average Apply Latency, Rollback Rate. Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/optimize-apply.
- SLOs: 99% apply success within 30s for control-plane only operations, 95% for Dedicated pool rollouts.

Open questions & decisions:
- Q: Should we allow server-side generated idempotency when client omits key? A: Decision: require client-supplied idempotency to avoid accidental dedupe across independent recs.
- Q: Force apply API surface? A: Expose POST /apply?force=true only for users with role=automation-admin; requires audit log and 2FA for Console.

Progress updates (log):
- 2025-02-18: Ticket created and initial design sketched in PRD.
- 2025-02-20: Spike finished; verified idempotency table shape and op_hash semantics.
- 2025-02-25: Prototype of apply endpoint and in-memory idempotency store merged to internal branch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/1289
- 2025-03-01: Webhook adapter landed as library; control-plane now emits apply.* events to webhook endpoints. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/904
- 2025-03-04: Begin integration tests against dedicated-staging-3; found race where duplicate idempotency_key from retries with different op_hash returned 200 incorrectly — fix planned in next sprint.

Next steps / Acceptance criteria:
- API contract docs merged in OpenAPI under optimize-api v1. (doc PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/openapi/pull/412)
- End-to-end tests green for stepwise Dedicated rollout and rollback.
- SDK helpers published (npm @redwood/optimize-sdk v0.6.0) and used by Console automation.
